cases.name: infix_prefix_within_word
cases.description: Query is a prefix fragment of a longer indexed token ('synth' inside 'synthase') — proves substring matching works within a word, not just whole tokens.

cases.name: reverse_substring_key_in_query
cases.description: Query is LONGER than the indexed token ('synthases' vs indexed 'synthase') -- proves the 'key in token' direction of matching is active, not just 'token in key'. This is a real, verified behavior, not hypothetical.

cases.name: case_insensitive
cases.description: Uppercase query must return identical results to the lowercase version.

cases.name: multi_token_and
cases.description: Two-word query — both tokens must match (AND), not OR. 'atp synthase' should score real ATP synthase subunit names at the top via the whole-phrase substring-in-name relevance tier (score 2).

cases.name: exact_annotation_id
cases.description: Exact ID match should score highest (tier 4) but the result set is NOT just that one ID -- short substrings of the query (e.g. 'co', 'g005') are themselves indexed keys from unrelated annotations' names, so they get swept in at lower tiers. This is real, verified behavior, not a hypothetical.

cases.name: id_prefix_no_exact_match
cases.description: Prefix of several real IDs (COG0050-COG0059) with no exact match itself -- exercises the 'annotation_id starts with query' tier-2 rule.

cases.name: single_character_query
cases.description: Extreme short-query case -- matches nearly every annotation via substring. Any replacement engine needs an explicit policy for this (Mike's review: 'require 3+ chars for infix, or bounded fallback').

cases.name: no_match
cases.description: Genuine zero-match query, verified: a repeated character long enough to escape substring matching in both directions. Note this is HARDER to achieve than it sounds -- see 'surprising_substring_collision' below.

cases.name: surprising_substring_collision
cases.description: Looks like a nonsense query, but real behavior: matches 139 results in production. 'A' is a standalone whitespace-tokenized word in real names like 'Arylsulfatase A or related enzyme' -- since this query contains the letter 'a', the reverse-substring rule (key-in-token) matches every annotation with a bare single-letter word token anywhere in its name. Verified: single letters b/f/k/q/w/x/z each independently match 190-2457 results on their own. This means almost no alphabetic query can return zero results, not just short ones -- a materially bigger problem than the documented '1-2 character query' case alone.

cases.name: cross_source
cases.description: Same query across all four sources in one request. sources= is a repeated FastAPI list param (?sources=a&sources=b), not comma-joined -- caught as a real bug in this fixture script itself (silently returned 0 results before the fix).
